title: Tributary lifecycle event on _tb.<env>.events, v0
description: One JSON object per record. See README.md. Producers validate strictly; consumers ignore unknown fields and higher 'v' values rather than failing.

kind.$comment: 'record' identifies a Kafka record that could not be identified as a Tributary message at all - undecodable or unparseable headers - so it is described by its topic/partition/offset coordinates instead of by tb-msg-id. Without it, the one record class most likely to mean an attack or a broken producer would be visible only in logs, which is the surface invariant 6 most restricts.

correlation_id.$comment: UUID only, engine-minted. It reaches ClickHouse and the browser in clear text, so it must not be derivable from a patient identifier or any payload field.

claim_check.$comment: Same rules as tb-claim-check: opaque locator, no query string, no fragment, no userinfo. Events are persisted to ClickHouse and rendered in the browser, so a presigned URL here becomes a stored, replayable credential.

error_message.description: Redacted static text. Never str(exception), never payload bytes (invariant 6).

attrs.description: Searchable metadata. Identifier-derived entries MUST use an _hmac suffix and a 64-hex-character value; a name known to denote a direct identifier is rejected in clear form. Other values are short low-cardinality codes: no spaces, 64 characters max, and no HL7 delimiter characters (| ^ ~ \ &) or CR/LF, so a segment cannot be pasted in. Producers must also keep the whole attrs object under 1024 serialized bytes, which JSON Schema cannot express. This RAISES THE COST of smuggling payload into attrs; it does not make it impossible.

allOf.$comment: Deny-list of names that denote a direct identifier. These are only admissible hashed, i.e. as <name>_hmac. This catches the common mistake; it is not a proof, so code review and security-reviewer remain the real control.

_hmac$.$comment: Fixed-length lowercase hex only, so a clear-text value cannot hide behind an _hmac suffix. WARNING: this shape does NOT prove the value is a keyed hash — an unkeyed SHA-256 digest is also 64 hex characters. The hashing mechanism itself is UNRESOLVED and escalated to a human via ADR-004; see README section 3.1.

allOf.$comment: Message events identify a message and use only message stages.
Partition events identify a partition and use only partition stages.

Record events describe an UNIDENTIFIABLE record by its Kafka coordinates. message_id, when present, is the id the engine minted for the quarantine wrapper it wrote to the DLQ - never a value read out of the broken record, which is untrusted input. channel is the channel whose topic it was read from, which is known from the subscription rather than from the record.

not.$comment: No attrs on a quarantine event. Every attrs value would have to be derived from the broken record's own bytes, and attrs become searchable columns in ClickHouse and the browser - the one place the contract cannot let unvalidated input land.

content_type.$comment: Unknown by definition. Naming it octet-stream keeps the field honest rather than guessing from a header that could not be read.

allOf.$comment: A failure must name a machine-readable cause, or alerting cannot group it.
A claim-checked payload has no inline bytes.
